about.title: How drills work
about.subtitle: What a drill is, how to solve each type and what the board expects from you.
about.intro: A drill is a short single-position exercise. Unlike classical puzzles, which often require a long forced sequence, here you respond in one move or one click — the goal is to spot the pattern fast, almost on reflex. The board is static, no one moves for either side. Seven drill types are currently live, each with its own check.
about.modesNote: Beyond single-position practice there's a sprint — a mix of drills against a 3- or 5-minute clock with leaderboards — and a daily drill delivered through the Telegram bot.
tips: Don't reach for complicated solutions — a drill is always about one simple pattern.
After a mistake you get about a second and a half to study the highlighted correct answer. If your system is set to reduce motion, position transitions are instant.
"Back" and "Forward" buttons let you scroll through the last ten positions you've seen and re-check your answers.
"Sprint" mode mixes drill types — it's no longer studying, it's a speed check.

oneLiners.findHangingPiece: Capture the undefended enemy piece in a single move.
oneLiners.findLoosePiece: Find the opponent's piece that has no defenders at all.
oneLiners.findFork: Find the move that simultaneously attacks two valuable enemy pieces.
oneLiners.countAttackers: How many pieces of the given colour attack the highlighted square?
oneLiners.findAllChecks: Play every move that delivers check.
oneLiners.findUndefendedAttack: Find the move that leaves the opponent with a piece attacked and undefended — and keeps your attacking piece itself safe.

whatItTrains.findHangingPiece: The single most common amateur blunder is leaving a piece attacked and undefended. This drill builds the habit of spotting these gifts and grabbing them without delay. Asking yourself "what's hanging in the opponent's camp?" before every move noticeably improves results.
whatItTrains.findLoosePiece: An undefended piece is a potential target even if no one attacks it right now. This drill teaches you to spot the weak spots in the opponent's camp early — tactics begin with finding the target. Without this habit, half the combinations simply don't come to mind.
whatItTrains.findPin: A pin is when an opponent's piece can't move freely because a more valuable piece of its own colour — or the king — sits behind it on the same line. If the king is behind, the pin is absolute: the piece literally can't move. If a queen, rook, or other valuable piece is behind, the pin is relative: it can move, but the loss outweighs the gain. Spotting pins is both defence and attack — pinned pieces are easy targets to pile up on.
whatItTrains.findFork: A fork is one of the most common tactical ideas: one move attacks two (or more) valuable targets, and the opponent can't save both. Knights are especially good at it, but queens, rooks, bishops, and even pawns all fork. The drill requires you to create a new fork: hit two targets that this piece wasn't already attacking.
whatItTrains.countAttackers: Every trade calculation starts with counting attackers and defenders. Two White attackers vs. one Black defender — White can take. This drill builds the habit of seeing that number fast, without effort. Count everyone, including batteries (two rooks, or a rook + queen, lined up along the same file or rank) and pinned attackers — a pinned piece still attacks the square.
whatItTrains.findAllChecks: Checks are forcing — the opponent must react. Scanning all possible checks before every move is a coach-recommended habit and the foundation for finding tactics and mating attacks. Each position in this drill has between 2 and 7 distinct checking moves to find, including discovered checks and capture-checks.
whatItTrains.findUndefendedAttack: This drill is calculation one move ahead. Picture the board after your move and check: is there an enemy piece you now attack with no defenders covering it? Discovered attacks and bringing up a new attacker count too. Important: your attacking piece must stay safe — if it ends up under attack itself after the move, the drill won't accept it (that's no longer "hanging the opponent's piece", that's a blunder).

howToAnswer.findHangingPiece: Make a move on the board — either click "from → to" or drag your piece onto the hanging one.
howToAnswer.findLoosePiece: One click on the piece's square.
howToAnswer.findPin: One click on the pinned piece's square.
howToAnswer.findFork: Make a move on the board — click "from → to" or drag.
howToAnswer.findAllChecks: Play the moves on the board normally — each new check triggers a green flash, the piece is automatically returned to its starting square, and the counter increments. If a move doesn't give check, a red flash; the attempt counts. When all checks are found, the drill auto-completes.
howToAnswer.findUndefendedAttack: Make a move on the board — click "from → to" or drag.

findHangingPiece.text: Black to move. The White pawn on f4 is attacked by the Black king, and nobody defends it: the White king on e2 doesn't reach f4 and no other White pieces are around. The right move is Kxf4 — after the capture the Black king is safe. A clean material win.

findLoosePiece.text: White to move. We're hunting a Black piece with no defender. The Black king on b2 doesn't reach c4. There are no other Black pieces. Correct answer: c4 — a Black pawn with zero defenders.

findPin.text: Black to move. The Black queen on d4 attacks the White pawn on f2 along the d4–e3–f2 diagonal. Behind the pawn on the same diagonal stands the White king on g1. If the f2 pawn moves, it exposes the king. Correct answer: f2 — the pinned piece sits between the attacking queen and the king.

findFork.text: White to move. Black has: king on a1, rook on b3, pawn on a3. The White queen sits on d2. The right move is Qd1+ — the queen gives check along the 1st rank and at the same time attacks the rook on b3 along the d1–c2–b3 diagonal. Black has to deal with the check first; the rook is lost.

countAttackers.text: Highlighted square h6, counting White attackers. The h5 pawn covers g6, not h6. The g4 pawn covers f5/h5. The White knight on f5 covers d4, e3, e7, d6, g7, h4, h6, g3 — yes, h6 is on its list. No other White piece reaches h6. Correct answer: 1.

findAllChecks.text: White to move. The White rook on c2 has two checking moves: Rc6+ (placing the rook next to the king along the 6th rank) and Rd2+ (placing the rook on the same file as the king). Two unique target squares — c6 and d2 — that's the drill's minimum.

findUndefendedAttack.text: White to move. White: rook on b8, king on c4, pawn on a3. Black: king on c6, rook on e4, pawn on c7. The Black rook on e4 isn't currently attacked. Correct answer: Kc4-d3 — the White king steps to d3 and from there attacks the rook on e4 diagonally. Nobody can defend the rook: the Black king on c6 doesn't reach e4, and the c7 pawn only covers b6/d6. The king on d3 itself is safe: the Black rook stands on the 4th rank and the e-file, not d3, and the Black king on c6 is too far. The attacking piece (our king) stays safe — the move counts. A good reminder that in the endgame the king is an attacking piece too.

onboarding.title: What's this drill?
onboarding.showAgainHint: You can reopen the description at any time via the «?» button on the board.

body.findHangingPiece: Time to practise grabbing hanging pieces. There's an enemy piece on the board you attack and nobody defends. Make the move and take it.
body.findLoosePiece: Time to spot undefended pieces. One enemy piece on the board has zero defenders — find it and click its square. It doesn't have to be under attack right now; the absence of any defender is what counts.
body.findPin: Time to find pins. A pinned piece is one that can't move freely because a more valuable piece — or the king — sits behind it on the same line. Click on the pinned piece in the middle, between the attacker and what it shields.
body.findFork: Time to set up forks. A fork is a move after which one of your pieces simultaneously attacks two valuable enemy pieces, and the opponent can't save both. Find the move and play it on the board.
body.countAttackers: Time to practise counting attackers. A square will be highlighted and a colour shown — how many pieces of that colour attack this square? Press the button for 1, 2, 3, or 4. Count batteries along a line and pinned attackers too — they still attack the square.
body.findAllChecks: Time to find every check in the position. Play checking moves on the board one by one — each correct check is counted and the piece is returned to its starting square. Find them all: positions have between 2 and 7 checks. Don't miss discovered checks and capture-checks.
body.findUndefendedAttack: Time to practise one-move calculation. You need a move that leaves an enemy piece attacked and undefended afterwards — your piece hits it and no one can defend. Important: your attacking piece must stay safe itself — if it ends up under attack after the move, the drill won't count it.

engineHelp.title: How to Use External Engine
engineHelp.intro: Connect a powerful chess engine running on your computer to Kingside for deeper analysis. Follow these steps:
engineHelp.step1Desc: Download kingside-engine-bridge for your operating system from GitHub Releases.
engineHelp.step2Desc: Install Stockfish or another UCI-compatible chess engine on your computer.
engineHelp.step3Desc: Extract the archive and run the bridge binary. It will start a WebSocket server on port 9090.
engineHelp.step4Desc: Open config.yaml (created on first run) and copy the secret_key value.
engineHelp.step5Desc: Go to any analysis page, click the ⚙ gear icon in the engine panel, and select "External Engine".
engineHelp.step6Desc: Enter the WebSocket URL and your secret key from config.yaml.
engineHelp.step7Desc: Press Connect. The status indicator will turn green when connected. Your engine is now analyzing positions!
engineHelp.faqConfigDesc: The bridge creates config.yaml on first run. Below are correct examples for each operating system. Important: secret_key must always be in quotes (otherwise YAML parse error for hex values).
engineHelp.faqSecretKeyNote: Always wrap secret_key in quotes — hex strings like 5caa... may be misinterpreted by YAML without them.
engineHelp.faqWindowsPathNote: On Windows use .\  prefix for relative paths to the engine executable.

play.title: Play Online
play.description: Challenge players worldwide in bullet, blitz, rapid or classical. Play against bots (8 levels) to practice. Custom time controls available.
play.guide:
Play against other players or bots.

Online games:
1. Go to Lobby (home page)
2. Select time control: Bullet (1-2 min), Blitz (3-5 min), Rapid (10-15 min), Classical (30+ min)
3. Or create a custom time control with any initial time and increment
4. Click "Play" — matchmaking finds an opponent of similar rating
5. During the game: move pieces by dragging or clicking. Premove is supported — make your next move while opponent is thinking
6. After the game: click "Rematch" to play again with the same opponent

Bot games:
1. In the Lobby, switch to "Play Bot" tab
2. Choose difficulty level (1-20, where 1 is beginner and 20 is Stockfish at full strength)
3. Choose your color (White, Black, or Random)
4. Choose time control
5. Click "Play"

Watch live games:
Click "Live Games" in the menu to spectate ongoing games between other players.

Challenge a friend:
Visit a player's profile and click "Challenge". Choose time control and send the challenge.

analyze.title: Deep Analysis
analyze.description: Stockfish 18 runs in your browser — no downloads needed. Connect your own engine for unlimited depth. Get accuracy scores, move classifications, and eval graphs.
analyze.guide:
Analyze any chess position with Stockfish 18.

Basic analysis:
1. Go to Workshop > New Analysis, or click "Review" after a game
2. Click "Start" to activate the engine
3. The engine shows the best move and evaluation. Use +/− buttons to change the number of lines (MultiPV, 1-10)
4. Navigate moves with arrow keys or buttons. Click on any move in the notation to jump to that position

Variations:
- Make an alternative move on the board — it creates a variation branch
- Right-click a variation to promote or delete it

Game Report:
After a finished game, click "Analyze" to get a full report:
- Accuracy percentage for both players
- Each move classified: Brilliant (!!) / Best / Good / Inaccuracy (?!) / Mistake (?) / Blunder (??)
- Eval graph showing the advantage over time

Board Editor:
Click "FEN" button to open the position editor. Place pieces freely to analyze any position.

External engines:
Click the gear icon (⚙) in the engine panel to connect a stronger engine running on your computer via Engine Bridge.

Export:
Click "↓ PGN" to download the game with your analysis and variations.

Mobile:
On mobile, the screen splits into two panels below the board. Each panel has tabs (Moves / Engine) so you can see notation and engine lines simultaneously.

puzzles.title: Puzzles & Training
puzzles.description: Solve puzzles matched to your rating. Race against the clock in Puzzle Rush. Generate custom puzzles from any PGN — train on your own mistakes. Filter by theme: forks, pins, mates, sacrifices.
puzzles.guide:
Solve chess puzzles to improve your tactical vision.

Puzzles:
Go to Puzzles in the menu — the next puzzle is matched to your rating, with filters by theme and difficulty.

Puzzle Rush:
1. Go to Puzzle Rush in the menu
2. Choose time limit: 3 minutes or 5 minutes
3. Solve as many puzzles as possible before time runs out
4. Your best scores appear on the leaderboard

Generate Puzzles from Games:
1. Go to Puzzles (menu)
2. Click "Generate from PGN" at the top
3. Upload a .pgn file or paste PGN text
4. Open "Advanced Settings" to tune generation:
   - Depth (8-22): analysis depth, higher = better but slower
   - Lines (2-5): number of engine lines to compare
   - Gap (cp): minimum difference between best and second-best move
   - Max 2nd line (cp): skip positions where the alternative is already strong
   - Skip hanging captures: filter out trivial free-piece captures
   - Skip attacked by lesser: filter moves where the piece lands on a square attacked by a cheaper piece
   - Skip undefended after move: filter moves leaving the piece undefended
5. Click "Generate Puzzles" and wait for analysis
6. Review generated puzzles and click "Save to Server"

Solving:
The board shows the position — find the best move. After solving or failing, click "Next" for the next puzzle. Click "Analysis" to open the position in the analysis board.

workshop.title: Workshop
workshop.description: Import and manage PGN files. Save your analyses. Set up any position with the board editor.
workshop.guide:
Your personal chess workspace.

My Analyses:
Saved analyses appear here. Click any to continue where you left off. Each analysis preserves your variations and annotations.

PGN Files:
1. Go to Workshop > PGN Files
2. Click "Upload" to import a .pgn file
3. Click a file to see its games. Click a game to open it in the analysis board
4. Rename a file: click the pencil icon (✎) on the file card
5. Delete a file: click × on the file card (deletes all games inside)
6. Delete a single game: click × next to the game in the game list

broadcasts.title: Live Broadcasts
broadcasts.description: Watch top tournament games in real-time with engine analysis.
broadcasts.guide:
Watch live chess tournament games with real-time engine analysis.

1. Go to Broadcasts in the menu
2. Active tournaments appear in the list automatically
3. Click a tournament to see rounds, click a round to see games
4. Click a game to watch it live with the analysis board

social.title: Community
social.description: Add friends, see who's online, challenge them to a game. Direct messages. Real-time notifications.
social.guide:
Connect with other players.

Friends:
1. Visit a player's profile (Players page or search)
2. Click "Add Friend". They will receive a notification
3. Go to Friends page to see who's online. Online friends have a green dot
4. Click a friend's name to view their profile, or click "Challenge" to start a game

Messages:
Click the envelope icon in the header to open direct messages. Click a friend to start a conversation.

Notifications:
The bell icon in the header shows unread notifications: friend requests, challenges, game invitations. Click to view and manage.

Blocking:
On a player's profile, click "Block" to prevent them from messaging you or appearing in matchmaking.

customize.title: Personalize
customize.description: Choose your board theme. Adjust sounds and animations. Play in English or Russian.
customize.guide:
Personalize your experience.

Settings page (click your username > Settings):
- Board theme: Classic, Green, Blue, Brown
- Piece set: Standard, Cburnett, Alpha, Merida
- Notation: show/hide coordinates on the board
- Input mode: drag or click
- Sound effects: on/off
- Move animation speed
- Language: English or Russian

rating.title: Rating System
rating.guide:
Track your progress with Elo ratings.

- Separate ratings for each time control: Bullet, Blitz, Rapid, Classical, and Puzzles
- Starting rating: 1500
- Rating changes after each game based on the result and opponent's rating
- View your rating history chart on your profile page
- See other players' profiles: click their name anywhere in the app
- Players page shows all registered players sorted by rating
- Online counter in the header shows how many players are currently on the site
